new_in_run20.cross_run_coverage_persistence: At run END the agent persists the swept ground -- the visited player-cell set + fired-probe set + movement-frontier plateau -- as a game-scoped KB note (kb_protocol.encode_coverage_state: run-length-encoded columns per level|row, plus action:object probe tokens, plus a meta board/plateau line). The body is digit-heavy (it trips both the grid-dump write guard and the daemon source-cluster rewrite), so it rides the SAME chunked-note scheme as a program (index note + chunk notes each under CHUNK_BODY_LIMIT), superseding the prior coverage note so ground ACCUMULATES rather than forking. On run START the agent RESUMES: read_coverage_state resolves the index (native /note/get full-body first, else chunk reassembly under the count/byte-length invariant), seeds _coverage_cells + _fired_probes + _coverage_plateau, and records coverage_resumed_pct. Budgets never compound: the next run never re-sweeps persisted ground. A KB read miss/outage degrades cleanly to a fresh sweep.
new_in_run20.bump_probes: Run 19 PROVED ls20 exposes ONLY movement actions (ACTION1-4, all translations; non-movement vocabulary EMPTY), so the win must be contact/positional. When _non_movement_actions returns [], interaction discovery now falls back to CONTACT bump probes (_bump_discovery): for each adjacent distinct object class (segmentation hash, cheapest reach first), CPU-plan movement onto the empty approach cell beside it, then fire the movement action that steps INTO the object bump_probe_repeats=3 times, diffing each bump for ANY effect beyond blocked/no-op and the auto-changing region -- object moved/recolored/vanished, score delta, or newly reachable ground. The bump direction->action map is derived empirically by sampling multiple reachable model states (a single boxed-in cell hides directions). A found effect is recorded as a game-scoped interaction note and resets the coverage plateau (a bump may open new ground). Deduped by (<bump>, object_hash) through the SAME _fired_probes set that coverage persistence now carries across runs. New telemetry bumps_probed / bumps_found.

why_bumps_did_not_fire_live: Both Run-20 fixes LANDED and are proven in the test suite (coverage codec round-trips through the truncating daemon; a second toy run resumes persisted coverage with no re-visits; the push-block toy is solved END-TO-END by a contact bump; bump dedup respects persisted probes). But the LIVE run fired 0 bumps for a single, now-measured reason: bump discovery (like interaction discovery) engages ONLY after the movement frontier is declared exhausted -- real coverage plateaus for coverage_plateau_exhaust=2 CONSECUTIVE frontier batches. On the 80-action budget the ls20 sweep grows slowly (frontier_batches=11, coverage_pct=0.05, identical shape to runs 18/19) and each ~16-action batch endpoint still lands on a fresh cell, so the plateau never reaches 2-in-a-row before the budget is exhausted. The exhaustion gate never trips, so neither interaction probes nor bumps fire. Coverage persistence was designed to break exactly this (resume the plateau within one budget), but this run it could not engage: the daemon was degraded again and the coverage-state search TIMED OUT (coverage_resumed_pct=0.0, fresh sweep). Next lever: (a) lower coverage_plateau_exhaust to 1 or raise the action budget so the movement frontier plateaus within budget and hands off to bumps; and/or (b) a healthy daemon so the persisted coverage note actually resumes the plateau across runs.
